issue.title: Document that upgrades to 8.x must always go via 7.last

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Upgrading to the next major version with a rolling restart requires upgrading to the last minor of the previous major first. However you could upgrade from 5.x to 6.x and from 6.x to 7.x via a full cluster restart without upgrading to 5.last (respectively 6.last) first.

For 8.x we will impose the same restriction on both upgrade paths: they must always go via 7.last. This will ensure that folks are notified about all deprecations and other changes before starting the major upgrade. The docs for full cluster restart upgrades need to be modified to account for this change in policy.

/cc @skearns64

Relatedly, the 8.0 upgrade docs speak about upgrading from "7.x" in various places where really we mean "7.last". We should fix them too.

Relates #81865

issue.title: Recovering from 8.0 upgrade failure due to unmigrated 6.x indices

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The Stack Management team removed the system index migration feature from Upgrade Assistant in 7.16 (https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/119798). During upgrade testing, @LeeDr discovered that users who upgrade from 6.8 to 7.16 will use Upgrade Assistant to prepare their deployment for upgrade, skipping the system indices migration step. It's reasonable to assume that some portion of these users might believe that they can upgrade to 8.0 at this point, unaware that we expect them to upgrade to 7.17 first.

After upgrading to 8.0, Elasticsearch will fail to start for these users because of the unmigrated 6.8 system indices. This startup failure occurs after ES has updated the keystore to be 8.x compatible. A user who attempts to fix this problem by downgrading to 7.16 will be blocked from doing so due to keystore incompatibility with 7.x (this is my assumption and needs verification). The user is now stuck, unable to complete their upgrade.

We have many users still on 6.x and prior, increasing the risk of users encountering this scenario. @DaveCTurner suggested we file this issue as an 8.0 blocker.

Some solutions suggested by David:
* Run some checks before doing the reorg
* Revert the reorg later on
* Provide some tool support for reverting it

CC @elastic/kibana-stack-management
